video_title: Warriors Trading Porzingis? Should Nuggets Worry About Jokic’s Future? + Flagg’s Mavs on the Rise

quotes.speaker: Adam Mares
quotes.summary_phrase: Dallas Mavericks' strong performance and future outlook
quotes.excerpt: They've actually looked fantastic way more than they haven't, and the times they haven't looked great, often it's because someone's not in the lineup.
quotes.quote: They've actually looked fantastic way more than they haven't, and the times they haven't looked great, often it's because someone's not in the lineup. Their fully healthy team, it surprised me. I did not think this team would be able to hang even this late into the season with some of the better teams in the West. They're 11 and 7 as of the time of this recording.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Mavericks' performance and the impact of Jason Kidd and Kyrie Irving
quotes.excerpt: 11 and 4 when Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving are in the lineup together.

text_blocks.speaker: Marc Stein
text_blocks.text: I don't know anyone in this city where I reside who said, 'Yeah, they're going to be 11 and 7 going into the day after Thanksgiving trip to Phoenix.' No chance. 11 and 4 when Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving are in the lineup together. 9 and 0 when Cooper Flagg rumbles for 20 points, five rebounds and five assists or more. Jason Kidd as a first-year coach has made the jump, he has made it look very easy when history tells us it's not.

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: Dante Exum as a first-year coach has made the jump, he has made it look very easy when history tells us it's not.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Memphis Grizzlies' impressive start and injury challenges
quotes.excerpt: Memphis is the story in terms of Cinderellas in the first month of the season.
quotes.quote: Memphis is the story in terms of Cinderellas in the first month of the season to achieve what they achieved, winning their first eight road games and putting the ball in Tyus Jones' hands before they just lost Cam Bouzer to injury and they also lost Jeremy Grant to injury. The Grizzlies were rolling. They've been an unbelievable surprise.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Timberwolves' success without Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: Minnesota to win at the level they have without Anthony Edwards, with LaMelo Ball coming in there.
quotes.quote: Minnesota to win at the level they have without Anthony Edwards, with LaMelo Ball coming in there and leading that team without, he's supposed to be the sidekick who makes Ant's life easier and they're still winning without Ant and now maybe getting Dante DiVincenzo back shortly after the New Year, they've been a great story.

quotes.speaker: Adam Mares
quotes.summary_phrase: Dallas Mavericks' defensive strategy and execution
quotes.excerpt: They send a third defender over on pick and rolls with Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic.
quotes.quote: What I saw yesterday was a team that executed a thought, a very good defensive game plan. They send a third defender over on pick and rolls with Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic. A lot of teams will decide to let Murray and Jokic go or try to take one of those guys away but stay home on shooters. Don't let Denver shooters get going. I thought Dallas did a great job in that game on Tuesday of really packing the paint, overloading, but they have the speed and length to close out on shooters.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May's coaching impact on the Mavericks
quotes.excerpt: It starts with a top two-some. Not unlike the Nuggets, when you have Flagg and Kyrie Irving.
quotes.quote: It starts with a top two-some. Not unlike the Nuggets, when you have Flagg and Kyrie Irving to build your game around, that certainly that puts you in every game right there. And for all the unsung heroes that the Mavs had in that game, in the fourth quarter, Kyrie Irving led the way with Cooper Flagg on the bench until basically, Kyrie Irving was exhausted and then Cooper Flagg came in for him and did the same thing, and they the two of them just made sure that the lead didn't go away. But look, we know Masayuki Ujiri who's been now in charge of the Mavericks since early May, he's always loved length, athleticism. Those are the kind of players he targets. Who did the Mavs target in the offseason in trade? They brought in Zachary Risacher to see if they can get his career back on track. That's the kind of player we know Masayuki Ujiri likes to go after.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May's coaching philosophy and team adaptability
quotes.excerpt: He doesn't get ruffled. He's been very steady and he clearly believes in himself.
quotes.quote: He doesn't get ruffled. He's been very steady and he clearly believes in himself and like, you know, has not come into this as, you know, the last college coach was John Beilein, also from Michigan, that he didn't last 60 games in Cleveland. Like, more often than not, the college to the pros jump is very, very bumpy, but like, I've most been struck by, he's very confident in what he's doing and does not get knocked off stride. And the way they have rebounded from a really bad opening night to what we see now, it's, you know, it is one of the better, I'm not going to say best, like I said, Memphis and Minnesota have also really been great stories in the West, but the Mavs are right there.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.excerpt: You saw his best game, his most important performance, the dunk in transition.
quotes.quote: You saw his best game, his most important performance, the dunk in transition, the all and look, my DLS Mavs colleagues will tell you that I've been too hard on him at the start, and it is true that for young big men making the transition from college to the NBA, it is difficult. He's also had shin splints and he was dealing with lower leg stuff in Summer League. So, my, you know, there were so many underwhelming performances early that my thought was, if he's not right, just sit him. Like this is not doing him any favors, but he's played through it. He's been great here of late. He's stacked two, three, two, three good games in a row.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Dallas Mavericks' draft decision and player development
quotes.excerpt: The Mavs had their choice basically of three Michigan men and Braden Burris. Like that was the choice.
quotes.quote: The Mavs had their choice basically of three Michigan men and Braden Burris. Like that was the choice. And Dusty May actually insists that he had no input on the pick. Now, he was hired basically coinciding with the draft. But let's be clear here. Again, three players who played for Dusty May and Braden Burris. That's basically who the Mavs were choosing from. Those were the four guys they were choosing from. Like they have to get this right. And going into the draft, no one was expecting the pick to be Moras Johnson Jr. So, Axel Lendeborg has had some amazing moments early in the season in Golden State, ditto for Adama Mara in Oklahoma City. Burris is in a really tough situation with a Bucks team that's just a mess. The point is, it's way too soon to judge Moras Johnson Jr., but like, Dallas has to have gotten this one right.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyrie Irving's role and team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: Cooper Flagg spent so much of his rookie season without proven guard play around him.
quotes.quote: One, Cooper Flagg spent so much of his rookie season without proven guard play around him. And I think he just loves that now someone as accomplished as Kyrie Irving is at his side almost every night. Also an underrated factor here, Kyrie Irving didn't play last season, but he did spend a fair amount of time in the practice facility getting on court with Cooper Flagg as much as he could. The decision was made, I want to say if my memory is right in late February, that Kyrie wasn't going to come back and decide to sit out the whole season, but they did get some practice floor time and and so it's not like they were starting from scratch when this season started. But the third thing and probably most important factor, Kyrie Irving can play with anybody. He's such a great plug and play player.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.excerpt: Trade season realistically starts December 15th when the bulk of last summer's free agents become trade eligible.
quotes.quote: Trade season realistically starts December 15th when the bulk of last summer's free agents become trade eligible, but yes, there is already a fair bit of trade discussion percolating because there are a lot of teams that are off to, to put it charitably, bumpy starts.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City Thunder's trade for Nick Clifford
quotes.excerpt: The Thunder swung one, the Thunder after losing Jaylen Williams, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren in quick succession.
quotes.quote: The Thunder swung one, the Thunder after losing Jaylen Williams, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren in quick succession, they went right out and acquired Nick Clifford from Sacramento. And yes, trade season realistically starts December 15th when the bulk of last summer's free agents become trade eligible, but yes, there is already a fair bit of trade discussion percolating because there are a lot of teams that are off to, to put it charitably, bumpy starts.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden State Warriors' trade strategy and Kristaps Porzingis
quotes.excerpt: Golden State is known to want to turn Kristaps Porzingis contract into a big man.
quotes.quote: Golden State is known to want to turn Kristaps Porzingis contract into a big man who can help them. But the Warriors are trying to thread a really tough needle where they want a player back who makes less than 20 million but can make an impact and they have to find a trade partner that just wants financial relief because Kristaps Porzingis, wherever he goes, he's not going to be playing and contributing. He really is just a team-friendly contract that the team is inheriting because most likely wherever Kristaps Porzingis goes, there will be buyout discussions to follow.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Philadelphia 76ers' trade limitations due to luxury tax
quotes.excerpt: The Sixers need another big man, but the Sixers because of luxury tax apron concerns.
quotes.quote: The Sixers need another big man, but the Sixers because of luxury tax apron concerns, they can't just sign somebody. They have to wait until early December so it doesn't take them into undesired apron territory. The Nuggets lost the Kevin Porter Jr. sweepstakes to Orlando because of apron concerns. The Nuggets have been showing interest in Kevin Porter Jr. for a while now. If you remember, Jake Fischer reported on my Substack before the Bucks waived Kevin Porter Jr. right at the roster cutdown deadline, Denver basically offered three first three second-round picks with Zeke Nnaji to get Kevin Porter Jr. and Milwaukee turned that down.

quotes.speaker: Marc Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic's future and trade rumors
quotes.excerpt: He can say it as much as he wants, but the reality is you're not going to stop.
quotes.quote: He can say it as much as he wants, but the reality is you're not going to stop other teams from lusting after him, even if it's a 5% chance, even if it's a 1% chance. It's Nikola Jokic. I mean, he's one of the best players on earth. Like, these teams, if they even sniff the smallest amount of hope, they're going to hope. And the reality is, Jokic, and I give him a lot of credit for this, he has said it as strongly as you can, 'I'm signing here, if the Nuggets want me, I'm signing here. I'm a Nugget forever.' He's said it over and over and over again, far more definitively than Giannis ever said it in Milwaukee. But the inescapable reality is two summers in a row, he has not done his extension. He's had an extension on the table, he didn't do it. All the whispers are that it's financially motivated, but to, you know, Jokic is eligible next summer for the richest contract ever. I think it's 350 over five. But to get that, he has to go all the way to unrestricted free agency.
